# Agent Reliability Skills MCP server

Forge Claude Code skills generate more reliable agents.

Agent Reliability Skills is the MCP server for Trustabl Forge. It writes a pre-coding reliability skill for **your**
repository: Forge reads the repository's dependency manifests (`package.json`, `pyproject.toml`, `requirements.txt`,
`go.mod` and others), finds the agent SDKs it uses, and builds a `SKILL.md` from Trustabl's detection rules for
exactly those SDKs. An agent that reads the skill applies the rules while it writes code, instead of meeting them
later as findings in a scan.

The skill is generated per repository. It is not a fixed skill to install, and it changes as your dependencies
and Trustabl's rules change.

Supported SDKs include the Claude Agent SDK, OpenAI Agents SDK, Google ADK, MCP, LangChain and LangGraph, CrewAI,
Pydantic AI, the Vercel AI SDK and AutoGen.

## Install

Requires Node.js 22 or later. Every install below downloads the release file from GitHub.

### Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add agent-reliability-skills -- npx -y https://github.com/trustabl/agent-reliability-skills/releases/download/v0.1.0-rc.1/agent-reliability-skills-0.1.0-rc.1.tgz
```

### Cursor

Add to `.cursor/mcp.json` in your project, or `~/.cursor/mcp.json` for every project:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "agent-reliability-skills": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "https://github.com/trustabl/agent-reliability-skills/releases/download/v0.1.0-rc.1/agent-reliability-skills-0.1.0-rc.1.tgz"]
    }
  }
}
```

### Claude Desktop

Open **Settings → Developer → Edit Config** and add the same `mcpServers` entry to
`claude_desktop_config.json`, then restart Claude Desktop.

Claude Desktop has no project folder, so name the repository when you ask, for example: *"Generate the Trustabl
pre-coding skill for /Users/me/code/my-agent and write it to .claude/skills/trustabl-pre-coding/SKILL.md."*

# jp-essay

**A Claude Code skill that runs Jordan Peterson's essay process, adapted to how models write.**

Question, reading list, outline, bad draft, outline from memory, reorder, rewrite, ask again.

**[Website](https://jpessay.com/)** · **[Read a sample essay](https://jpessay.com/sample.html)**

---

Peterson's [writing guide](https://essay.app/guide) is built for students, whose problem is skipping the work: no question, no reading, no outline, one draft. A model has the opposite problem. It does every step fluently and still produces generic prose: no claim worth arguing, no specifics, inflated words, hedged verdicts and an ending that summarizes. `jp-essay` keeps Peterson's steps and aims each one at the model's failure. A script checks every step, so the model can't skip one and say it's done, and no model grades the prose, because models asked to judge writing barely beat chance and reward overwriting.

> **Not affiliated with Jordan Peterson.** `jp-essay` is an independent project. Jordan B. Peterson has not reviewed or endorsed it. It is an iteration of the method in his writing guide, adapted for AI agents.

## Why I built this

AI agents are good at building things. They are also surprisingly good at
declaring something finished when it isn't. A requirement gets paraphrased in

# 🎞️ broll-mcp

**Find, preview and cut public-domain b-roll from the Internet Archive, from inside any MCP agent.**

Every clip lands on disk with a provenance record next to it: source, license, exact segment and attribution text.

---

```text
You:    "I need 8 seconds of children eating bananas, ideally black and white."

Agent → search_footage("children eating bananas")       5 ranked items, license + tier on each
Agent → inspect_item("AboutBan1935")                    scenes with a keyframe image per scene
Agent → extract_clip("AboutBan1935", start_s=300, 8s)   verified H.264 MP4 + provenance JSON
Agent → get_provenance(clip_id)                         "About Bananas" (1935), Prelinger Archives
                                                        via Internet Archive · Public Domain
```

The agent sees the footage before it cuts: `inspect_item` returns real keyframe images, so a vision model can pick the shot instead of guessing from titles.

## Why

archive.org holds decades of public-domain film (Prelinger, NASA, newsreels, stock footage), but using it from an agent is awkward:

- Raw item metadata can exceed **1 MB** for one item. That's a huge token cost before you've seen a single frame.
- Licenses differ **per item**, even inside one collection.
- Clips cut with `-c copy` snap to keyframes. An 8 s request came back as **11.35 s**.

# Zag

Accessible component logic for React, Vue, Solid, and Svelte.

Build dialogs, menus, comboboxes, date pickers, and more with state machines that handle keyboard interactions, focus

# Keyline Icons

**1,692 icons, drawn on one 24×24 grid, in four styles and two corner
treatments.** Built for shadcn/ui, free under MIT.

[**keylineicons.com**](https://keylineicons.com) to browse and copy.

| Style | Icons | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `stroke` | 1,692 | The full set. 2px keylines on a 24 grid. |
| `two-tone` | 1,692 | The stroke drawing over a flat plate at reduced opacity. |
| `duotone` | 1,692 | No outline: a grey body with the detail in full strength. |
| `fill` | 1,692 | Solid, with the detail knocked back out of the shape. |

`stroke` is the drawing every other style starts from, and since 1.0.0 every
name comes in all four. `two-tone` is what `duotone` meant until 0.9.0: the
outline kept, a 40% plate under it. `duotone` now drops the outline and decides
per icon which part is grey and which is black, so the thing that matters reads
first: the check on a badge, the liquid in a flask, the data rather than the
chart's axes. A glyph with nothing to fill, like `bar-chart`, carries its stroke
drawing in the filled styles, so no import ever comes up empty.

## Rounded and sharp

Every drawing in the table comes twice: rounded, with round caps and filleted
corners, and sharp, with butt caps and square corners. Same names, same
coverage, so 13,536 SVGs in total.

```

icons/sharp/stroke/bell.svg
icons/sharp/fill/bell.svg
```

solved again, so both treatments sit side by side in `raw/` and the build
converts neither into the other.

Convert a WordPress site to static Astro with your coding agent, and get back the same site: the

# better-skill

> **AI Agent 技能的医生手册。**

[🇺🇸 English](README.en.md) | **🇨🇳 中文**

---

你的 Agent 技能越多，越需要一个医生。

大多数技能仓库教你怎么**写**技能；这一份管的是标准：动工前该选哪种架构、一个健康技能内部长什么样、以及怎么用数字证明一个技能比另一个好。

## 为什么需要它

**Skill 可能做了几十个，但从来没有认真体检过一个。**

三个你大概熟悉的场景：

1. **技能写完就用，从没体检过。** 描述膨胀、方法内嵌正文、示例缺失——都是慢性病，发作的时候你只觉得"这技能不好用"，但说不出哪里坏。
2. **触发是玄学。** 该触发的时候不触发，不该触发的时候乱触发。几乎没人真的测过触发率——本标准把"描述触发"变成可以量化、可以迭代优化的工程问题。
3. **"我的技能比你的好"——没有统一标尺的对比就是吵架。** 五维标尺（ZSAR / 触发率 / 往返次数 / Token 占用量 / 自治等级）让对比有裁判。

## 30 秒上手

```bash
# 1. 克隆到你的技能目录（任何按 SKILL.md 加载技能的环境都可以）
git clone https://github.com/YTruman/better-skill.git <你的技能目录>/better-skill
```

```text
2. 对你的 Agent 说：
   "用 better-skill 体检一下我的 xx 技能"
3. 你会拿到：一份带证据行号的体检报告
```

（后续）一行命令安装与 YAI CLI 分发通道准备中——装一次，持续享受更新。

## 四种门诊，一条管线

| 模式 | 你说…… | 发生什么 | 你拿到什么 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **创建** | "我想做个新技能" | 范式选型 → 自由度定级 → 目录蓝图 → 施工 → 评测闭环 → 触发优化 | 一个带评测数据的新技能 |
| **体检** | "审计这个技能" | 四层 P0/P1/P2 扫描 + Not-To-Do 红线清单 | 体检报告：每个发现带证据行号与优先级 |
| **处方** | "升级这个技能" | 先出体检报告 → 只开 `str_replace` 级靶向补丁 | 最小 diff 补丁 + 复诊前后对比 |
| **会诊** | "哪个技能更好？" | 五维标尺统一度量 | 雷达对比表 + 保留/合并/退役建议 |

核心纪律：**先诊断，后开方。没有体检报告，禁止动刀。** 一条处方若指不回体检报告的具体条目，就是医疗事故。

## 一份真实体检长什么样

见 [`examples/perfect-audit-report.md`](examples/perfect-audit-report.md)：一次真实的四技能体检，抓出 6 项发现（全清单见 provenance『实战验证』节；示例文件为报告样式节选）——从 P0 的"缺初始对话协议"（方向跑偏风险），到一条刻意的"**不改动**"裁决（描述性中文是对话型技能的设计意图，不是缺陷）。

作者自己的用法：用它回头评审过去在 Codex、Claude Code 里封装的各个技能——看得一身冷汗。一个被 Agent 自查过好几轮、觉得已经无限完美的技能，在体检面前照样暴露出缺初始对话协议、缺触发关键词、缺任务路由。「怪不得我的工作流经常不稳定。」

知道什么时候不动刀，才是医生。

## 凭什么信这套标准

- **官方 300+ 技能全量审计**：332 个官方技能的调用模式逐一盘点，优先级从真实用法里排出来，不凭口味；

# pngdeer

**Smaller PNGs. Same picture.** pngdeer is a lossy PNG compressor with no quality slider: for each image it searches palette sizes from 2 to 256 colors, with and without dithering, scores each result with a perceptual metric, and keeps the smallest file that still looks right. brew install heydeer/tap/pngdeer
